evidence.summary: Kernel run on GPU over 107,010 inputs (extremes 0/4294967295, all multiples-of-7±1 at chosen quotients including max quotient, random 100k, full ranges [0,5000) and top 2000) matched the int64 reference exactly with zero mismatches and satisfied 7*row+col==index for all. Additionally, the kernel's exact formula ((v+1)*M)>>34 with M=2^34//7 was exhaustively verified equal to floor(v/7) and v%7 for ALL 2^32 unsigned values, with no failures. The reciprocal-multiplication implementation is exact over the entire legal domain.

rationale: The "+1 multiplier" reciprocal trick can be off-by-one if the multiplier/shift are miscomputed for the full uint32 range; contract requires exact coordinates for every value 0..4294967295.

scope_evidence.summary: EVERY unsigned 32-bit value is legal, 0 through 4294967295; every coordinate must equal the integer mathematical target EXACTLY, with 7*row+col equal to the original index.

scope_rationale: Contract requires exact row/col for every uint32 value including extrema; if the reciprocal-multiply formula is off by one for any value, this violates the exactness requirement.
statement: The kernel's reciprocal-multiplication quotient ((value+1)*MULTIPLIER)>>34 is not exactly floor(value/7) for some legal uint32 values, producing wrong row/col coordinates.
